Up Next

The next live episode

Episode 5 · Monday, October 19, 2026 · 1:00–2:00 PM PT

"On Leadership" — Part Four: Be a Leader

The final part of How to Win Friends and Influence People — "Be a Leader: How to Change People Without Giving Offense or Arousing Resentment." How do you correct someone, lead a team, or give hard feedback without making an enemy? Carnegie closes the book with nine principles for changing people while keeping their dignity — and their friendship — intact.

Live on KSSU · Catch it live — show recordings aren't posted, per station policy

How the hour runs

  1. Introduction talk — DJ Sat opens the show on KSSU and sets up today's topic: leadership.
  2. Topic talk segments — the 9 principles of Part Four, grouped in three talks: "Start with Praise" (principles 1–3 — praise and honest appreciation first, mistakes pointed out indirectly, your own mistakes admitted first), "Ask, Don't Order" (principles 4–6 — questions instead of direct orders, let people save face, praise every improvement), and "Bring Out the Best in People" (principles 7–9 — a fine reputation to live up to, encouragement that makes the fault seem easy to correct, and making people happy to do what you suggest). Carnegie's idea first, then DJ Sat's own view and examples.
  3. Clean songs between segments — "Sucker" (Jonas Brothers), "Golden Brown" (The Stranglers), "Message in a Bottle" (The Police), "505" (Arctic Monkeys), and "Say It Ain't So" (Weezer) — plus station drops and PSAs between the talk segments, KSSU-style (see the music policy).
  4. Closing recap talk — the principles in short, and the one takeaway to carry into the week.

The 9 principles of Part 4

  1. Begin with praise and honest appreciation.
  2. Call attention to people's mistakes indirectly.
  3. Talk about your own mistakes before criticizing the other person.
  4. Ask questions instead of giving direct orders.
  5. Let the other person save face.
  6. Praise the slightest improvement — and praise every improvement.
  7. Give the other person a fine reputation to live up to.
  8. Use encouragement; make the fault seem easy to correct.
  9. Make the other person happy about doing the thing you suggest.
"Good leadership isn't just telling people what to do — it's helping people improve without destroying their confidence or creating resentment." The closing takeaway of this episode

Fundamental Techniques in Handling People

The Carnegie series opens. Why criticism almost never works, why honest appreciation changes everything, and the one secret to getting people to want to do what you ask.

3Episode

Part Two · 6 principles · Aired Mon Oct 5, 2026 · as "The Sat Effect"

Six Ways to Make People Like You

The simplest social skills nobody teaches: genuine interest, listening more than you talk, and why a person's name is the sweetest sound they know. This show aired under the playlist title "The Sat Effect."

See the 6 principles
  1. Become genuinely interested in other people.
  2. Smile.
  3. Remember that a person's name is, to that person, the sweetest and most important sound in any language.
  4. Be a good listener — encourage others to talk about themselves.
  5. Talk in terms of the other person's interests.
  6. Make the other person feel important — and do it sincerely.

4Episode

Part Three · 12 principles · Aired Mon Oct 12, 2026 · as "The Sat Effect"

How to Win People to Your Way of Thinking

You can't win an argument — so what do you do instead? DJ Sat worked through Part Three in four talk segments, with clean songs in between. This show also aired under the playlist title "The Sat Effect."

The talk segments

  • Handling Disagreements
  • Let People Participate
  • Understanding Their Perspective
  • Making Your Ideas Powerful
See the 12 principles
  1. The only way to get the best of an argument is to avoid it.
  2. Show respect for the other person's opinions. Never say "You're wrong."
  3. If you are wrong, admit it quickly and emphatically.
  4. Begin in a friendly way.
  5. Get the other person saying "yes, yes" immediately.
  6. Let the other person do a great deal of the talking.
  7. Let the other person feel that the idea is his or hers.
  8. Try honestly to see things from the other person's point of view.
  9. Be sympathetic with the other person's ideas and desires.
  10. Appeal to the nobler motives.
  11. Dramatize your ideas.
  12. Throw down a challenge.

The Bookshelf

Books DJ Sat has read — and reads on air

The Sat Show runs on great books. These are the self-improvement reads on DJ Sat's own shelf — the books behind the episodes, the coaching, and the Monday conversations about habits, leadership, and becoming who you want to be. One of them is on air right now.

Dale Carnegie · 1936

How to Win Friends and Influence People

The classic that basically invented the genre — handling people, making friends, winning others to your way of thinking, and leading without resentment. The show's first full series, one part per episode.

On air now · Episodes 2–5

Joseph Murphy · 1963

The Power of Your Subconscious Mind

Murphy's classic on the subconscious — how the thoughts you quietly repeat shape your habits, your confidence, and the results you keep getting.

Read · On the shelf

Robin Sharma · 2018

The 5 AM Club

A fable about owning your morning — the 5 AM routine Sharma credits with the focus, energy, and calm behind world-class work.

Read · On the shelf

Robin Sharma · 2010

The Leader Who Had No Title

A modern fable with a simple claim: you don't need a title to be a leader — just the choice to do excellent work and lift the people around you.

Read · On the shelf

Robin Sharma · 2006

The Greatness Guide

Short, practical lessons on personal and professional greatness — small chapters, big habits, drawn from Sharma's coaching playbook.

Read · On the shelf

About

About the show — and DJ Sat

The Sat Show is a self-improvement hour on Sacramento State's student-run radio station, KSSU. Every Monday from 1:00 to 2:00 PM Pacific, DJ Sat takes one great book — or one great guest — and turns it into practical ideas you can use the same day: how to talk to people, how to lead, how to build better habits, and how to keep growing on purpose.

The current series works through Dale Carnegie's How to Win Friends and Influence People, the 1936 classic that basically invented the self-improvement genre. Coming next: guest episodes, where students and everyday people come into the studio and share the experiences that actually changed them.

DJ Sat is Satyam Bali — a computer science student at Sacramento State and a KSSU DJ. He started the show because the books that were changing his own life felt too good to keep to himself. His style on the mic: honest, curious, and practical — no guru talk, just ideas, stories, and the attempt to live them out loud, one week at a time.

  • Every Monday, 1:00–2:00 PM PT — live on KSSU at Sacramento State
  • Books, broken down live — one part, one principle set at a time
  • Real guests, real stories — experience episodes are coming
  • Clean radio, always — every song on the show is radio-safe

On the Mic

Request to Be a Guest — Schedule an Interview

Want to come on the show? The next chapter of The Sat Show is people — come share your story and your experience on the self-improvement podcast, live on KSSU Mondays 1:00–2:00 PM PT. DJ Sat is inviting guests into the studio to talk about the setback, the lesson, the comeback — so listeners can learn from real stories, not just books.

  1. Send the short form — or email satyambali@csus.edu — with your name and the story you'd share.
  2. DJ Sat replies — to pick a Monday that works and talk through your segment.
  3. Come to the studio — a relaxed live conversation on KSSU, Mondays 1:00–2:00 PM PT.
  • You don't need to be famous — students, workers, creators, anyone with a real story
  • One honest experience — something you lived that taught you something true
  • A relaxed conversation — DJ Sat asks the questions, you just talk

One friendly heads-up: guests are booked in advance — station guests get scheduled ahead of the show — so send your request early in the week to lock in your Monday.

The Music

Clean radio only

KSSU is a student station broadcasting under FCC rules, so every song on The Sat Show is checked before it airs. The rule is simple — if it wouldn't pass on daytime radio, it doesn't play here. Song requests are welcome, as long as they're clean.

✕

No profanity

No swear words or slurs — original or edited, every track is screened before air.

✕

No sexual or obscene content

No explicit, indecent, or obscene lyrics or themes — FCC and station rules apply to every song.

✓

Every song reviewed first

Each track is listened to and logged before broadcast. Clean requests from listeners are always welcome.

Show playlists and song logs are kept on Spinitron, KSSU's playlist system — public playlist pages for The Sat Show are coming soon.

Help It Grow

Ideas to make The Sat Show bigger

A campus radio show grows one listener at a time. Here's the playbook DJ Sat is working from — if you're a listener, the best help is simple: tune in Monday at 1, and send the show to one person who'd like it.

On Instagram Social

  • Principle of the Week — one Carnegie principle per post, every Monday morning before the show, so followers get the idea even if they miss the hour.
  • 60-second studio clips — short reels filmed in the booth: one idea, one story, one takeaway, ending with "Mondays 1 PM on KSSU."
  • Countdown & poll stories — a Monday countdown sticker, plus polls ("Which principle do you need most this week?") to pull listeners into the episode topic.
  • Guest collab posts — every guest episode gets a joint post with the guest, so their friends discover the show too.
  • Link in bio — this page as the bio link, so every post points to one home for episodes, coaching, and guest pitches.

On campus Sac State

  • Flyers with a QR code — dorms, the Union, and the library: "Mondays 1 PM. One hour. One idea that changes your week."
  • Club & class shout-outs — invite club leaders and student orgs as guests; their members become listeners.
  • Cross-promote with other KSSU DJs — guest spots and mentions on each other's shows.
  • Tabling at campus events — a small booth, the book of the month, and a mic so students can record a 10-second "best advice I ever got."

Make it a community Listeners

  • Listener question of the week — collect questions through Instagram and this page, answer one on air every show.
  • Book-of-the-month vote — after Carnegie, listeners vote on the next book the show reads together.
  • The 7-day principle challenge — each week, one principle to actually practice, with listeners reporting back on the next show.
  • Notes & essays page — DJ Sat's written show notes for each episode, posted here for listeners who want to go deeper.

Level up the show Craft

  • Keep the format tight — introduction talk, topic segments, clean songs, station drops & PSAs, closing recap: listeners always know the rhythm of the hour.
  • One strong guest a month — quality over quantity keeps every guest episode an event.
  • Ask every guest to share — one story post from each guest doubles the show's reach for free.
  • Review the tape — listen back each week, note what worked, and fix one thing per show.
